req.title: Reject wrong method on /put
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than PUT on /put.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /put must return HTTP 405 for any method other than PUT. We need: (1) a positive test confirming PUT returns 200, (2) negative tests confirming GET/POST/DELETE/PATCH return 405, and (3) boundary tests at the method-selection boundary (e.g., HEAD, OPTIONS). Each test uses exact status code assertions to catch comparison-operator mutations (== vs !=, 200 vs 405). We also verify the Allow header on 405 responses to catch mutations that suppress header logic. Tests are driven in-process via Flask test_client().

tests.name: test_put_method_returns_200_on_put_endpoint
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send HTTP PUT request to /put
expected: Response body is JSON containing url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json keys
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: PUT on /put must succeed with 2xx
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_put_method_returns_200_on_put_endpoint():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.put('/put')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in data

test_put_method_returns_200_on_put_endpoint()

tests.name: test_head_method_boundary_on_put_endpoint
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
HEAD is not in the allowed methods list for /put
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send HTTP HEAD request to /put
expected: HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed (HEAD is not PUT, so must be rejected)
Status code is exactly 405, not 200 or any 2xx
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: HEAD on /put must be rejected with 405 — boundary between allowed and disallowed methods
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_head_method_boundary_on_put_endpoint():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.head('/put')
    # HEAD is not PUT; Flask may return 200 for HEAD if PUT is allowed
    # but /put only allows PUT, so HEAD should be 405
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 200

test_head_method_boundary_on_put_endpoint()

tests.name: test_put_with_body_returns_200_and_correct_json_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send HTTP PUT request to /put with JSON body
expected: Response JSON contains exactly the keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: PUT on /put with body must return 200 with expected payload
tests.executable:
import json
from httpbin.core import app

def test_put_with_body_returns_200_and_correct_json_keys():
    client = app.test_client()
    payload = json.dumps({'key': 'value'})
    r = client.put(
        '/put',
        data=payload,
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    expected_keys = {'url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'}
    assert set(data.keys()) == expected_keys
    assert data['json'] == {'key': 'value'}

test_put_with_body_returns_200_and_correct_json_keys()

tests.name: test_all_non_put_methods_return_405_exhaustive
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send GET, POST, DELETE, PATCH requests to /put
Assert each returns exactly 405
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: Decision table — only PUT is allowed; all others must yield 405
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_all_non_put_methods_return_405_exhaustive():
    client = app.test_client()
    methods = [
        ('GET', client.get),
        ('POST', client.post),
        ('DELETE', client.delete),
        ('PATCH', client.patch),
    ]
    for method_name, method_fn in methods:
        r = method_fn('/put')
        assert r.status_code == 405, (
            f'{method_name} /put expected 405, got {r.status_code}'
        )
        assert r.status_code != 200, (
            f'{method_name} /put must not return 200'
        )

test_all_non_put_methods_return_405_exhaustive()

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_put_endpoint_405_response_has_allow_header():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/put')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    allow_header = r.headers.get('Allow', '')
    assert 'PUT' in allow_header
